title: Developer experience: SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples, docs site operating procedures, top support issues and canonical fixes
author: Aisha Patel
summary: Standards, templates, and operating procedures for Developer Experience documentation: SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples, docs site publishing, and canonical fixes for recurring top support issues.
body:
Purpose

This document defines the standard templates, review and publishing procedures, and canonical fixes for the most frequent support issues encountered by customers integrating Redwood SDKs and APIs. It centralizes best practices so engineering writers, SDK owners, and support engineers can produce consistent, reliable documentation and rapid fixes.

Scope

- SDK guides (Python, Node.js, Go)
- Quickstarts and reference templates for new integrations
- API examples (sync, streaming, embeddings, function-calling)
- Docs site operating procedures (publishing, release cadence, broken-link checks)
- Top support issues and canonical fixes (detection, triage, permanent fix template)

Ownership and contacts

- Primary owner: Developer Experience (DevEx) — Aisha Patel
- SDK maintainers: see SDK owners list (inline with each SDK guide)
- Support triage lead: Marco Alvarez

When to use this doc

- Creating a new SDK guide or quickstart (use templates below)
- Adding API examples to the docs site
- Responding to repeated support tickets (use canonical fixes)
- Running a docs-only release or emergency doc hotfix

Templates (copy-and-paste ready)

1) SDK Guide template (recommended sections)

- Title: <SDK name> Quickstart and Reference
- Short intro (1–2 sentences describing recommended surface)
- Installation (pip/npm/go install + recommended version pin)
- Authentication (how to set REDWOOD_API_KEY or use instance-specific base_url)
- Basic example (minimal code snippet to call API)
- Streaming example (if SDK supports)
- Error handling and common traps (401/429/timeout examples)
- Performance recommendations (batching, retry/backoff guidance)
- Migration notes (breaking changes between versions)
- Tests & asserts (example unit test for deterministic outputs)
- Files to include in repo: README.md, requirements.txt/package.json, example app

Example Python snippet to include under "Basic example":

```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")
resp = client.generate(model="rw-instruct-1", prompt="Summarize the release notes\")
print(resp.text)
```

Example JS snippet for async streaming example:

```javascript
import { Redwood } from '@redwood/inference'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
for await (const chunk of client.streamGenerate({ model: 'rw-chat-1', prompt: 'Write a short haiku' })) {
  process.stdout.write(chunk)
}
```

2) Quickstart README template

- Title & 1-line description
- Prereqs (account, API key, Node/Python version)
- 5-minute quickstart steps (clone, install, set env, run) — numbered list
- What to expect (example response snippet)
- Next steps (link to full SDK guide, troubleshooting)
- License and contributor notes

3) API Example Template (micro-doc for a single endpoint)

- Purpose: one-sentence description
- Inputs: required/optional params table (name, type, default, notes)
- Minimal example (Python + JS)
- Streaming variant (if applicable)
- Expected response schema (json shape example)
- Error modes and how to detect

Docs site operating procedures (publishing + day-to-day)

Goals: keep site stable, fast review-to-publish, and low regressions. Follow the steps below for any documentation change that will be served on the public docs site.

1) Authoring
- Use the SDK guide or Quickstart templates above.
- Add frontmatter at top of markdown: title, internal_id, sdk_tag, created_by, created_date. Example: 
  ---
  title: "Python SDK Quickstart"
  internal_id: devexp-python-quickstart-2026-10
  sdk_tag: python
  created_by: Aisha Patel
  created_date: 2026-10-01
  ---

2) Linting and pre-commit
- Run docs linter: yarn docs:lint (checks markdown style, broken links, frontmatter)
- Run example snippet test harness: yarn examples:test (executes snippets in a sandbox)

3) Pull request rules
- Require one technical reviewer (SDK owner) and one DevEx content reviewer.
- Include a preview link (staging docs URL) in PR description.
- Large breaking changes (API surface, CLI, major version) must include a migration guide and be flagged as "major-change" label.

4) CI checks
- Docs build: yarn docs:build must pass (no broken frontmatter)
- Link checks: no 4xx links to internal docs or external references
- Example tests: all code snippets must run in CI sandbox

5) Publishing cadence
- Minor doc fixes: merged -> auto-deploy to staging -> auto-deploy to prod within 30 minutes if no regressions
- Major docs release (API version change): scheduled release with announcement and rollback window (24 hours), coordinated with SDK releases

6) Emergency doc hotfixes
- Tag PR with "hotfix-doc" and ping #devex on Slack. Oncall SRE or DevEx lead will approve expedited deployment.

Quality gating and observability

- Every doc page must include metrics: last_updated, number_of_examples, automated_snippet_tests_passed (true/false).
- Staging site collects error telemetry for embedded examples (snippet timeouts, runtime errors). Generate weekly report for the Docs SRE board.

Top support issues and canonical fixes (canonicalized for support playbooks)

This section lists recurring issues reported in support tickets. For each issue we provide: symptom, likely root cause, immediate workaround, permanent fix steps, detection signals, and a small regression test to include in the SDK examples test harness. Use the templates below when creating a support KB article.

Issue 1: Authentication failures (401)\- Symptom: SDK calls return 401, often after successful calls earlier.\- Root cause(s): expired API key, environment variable not set in deployment, base_url misconfigured (pointing to private instance without valid token).\- Immediate workaround: confirm REDWOOD_API_KEY in process env; test with curl against /v1/auth/verify.\- Permanent fix: update onboarding quickstart to include: how to set env in common hosts (Heroku, Vercel, Dockerfile) and add automated check in SDK init that raises actionable error with link to KB.\- Detection: spike in 401 errors (monitoring alert: >5% 401s in 10m window)\- Regression test: include a unit test that asserts SDK raises an AuthError with explicit guidance when api_key missing.

Issue 2: Rate limit and throttling (429)\- Symptom: Customers hit 429 during peak traffic or misconfigured clients without backoff.\- Root cause: no retry/backoff in client, using synchronous loops without batching.\- Immediate workaround: enable exponential backoff, apply client-side rate limit using concurrency=2.\- Permanent fix: ship updated SDK with built-in retry/backoff default and recommended batching examples; update quickstart performance section.\- Detection: 429 rate > 0.5% of requests or repeating bursts from same client ID\- Regression test: stress test harness that simulates 200 requests/s and validates the SDK obeys client-side rate limit flag.

Issue 3: Streaming timeouts and truncated responses\- Symptom: Streaming requests stop mid-response, or websockets close unexpectedly.\- Root cause: intermediate proxies (corporate firewalls, load balancers) have aggressive idle timeouts; user uses TLS termination without proper keepalive.\- Immediate workaround: suggest short heartbeats or chunked keepalive messages and recommend use of the polling fallback for unstable networks.\- Permanent fix: add docs example showing how to implement keepalive in Node and Python streaming clients; include network recommendations in Private deployment guide.\- Detection: increase in aborted-stream telemetry and many partial-response support tickets\- Regression test: network-layer simulated test that drops connection after N seconds and asserts fallback behavior.

Issue 4: High latency for small prompts\- Symptom: 200–500ms overhead on every request, even for short outputs.\- Root cause: incorrect model selection (large LLM used for short deterministic tasks), missing caching/prefix KV cache, or HTTP/1.1 connection not reused.\- Immediate workaround: recommend model: rw-instruct-small or use cached completions for repeated prompts.\- Permanent fix: update quickstarts to include model selection table and enable connection pooling in SDK defaults.\- Detection: per-route p50 increased over baseline, token-level cost spike\- Regression test: latency bench that asserts p50 < 120ms for small prompt using recommended small model.

Issue 5: Embedding mismatches across languages\- Symptom: Semantic similarity scores inconsistent between English and non-English inputs.\- Root cause: wrong embedding model used, or normalization differences (accented char handling).\- Immediate workaround: recommend specifying language-aware embedding model and normalizing Unicode in client.\- Permanent fix: add explicit examples for utf-8 normalization in SDK examples and update product docs to call out model compatibility.\- Detection: user-reported quality regression; automated evaluation on multilingual prompt set degrades by >5%\- Regression test: add multilingual embedding QA to nightly eval harness.

Issue 6: SDK example breakage after minor SDK bump\- Symptom: Code examples in docs fail after a minor SDK release due to signature changes.\- Root cause: examples not covered by snippet tests in CI, or examples copy stale API surface.\- Immediate workaround: pin SDK version in examples until CI tests updated.\- Permanent fix: require examples:test in CI (already part of docs pipeline) and add pre-merge validation that examples import the new SDK version.\- Detection: CI docs-examples tests start failing post-release\- Regression test: example snippets executed against new SDK in a test sandbox before merging docs PR.

Issue 7: Private deployment base_url misconfigurations\- Symptom: SDK points at public host and fails with 403/404 for private deployment customers.\- Root cause: quickstart omitted instruction for setting REDWOOD_BASE_URL or the onboarding automation did not set host.\- Immediate workaround: add step in customer onboarding to run: export REDWOOD_BASE_URL=https://private.example.com and test with curl.\- Permanent fix: update quickstarts and the Private deployment onboarding checklist; add an SDK convenience flag --instance during CLI setup.\- Detection: support tickets labeled "private-deploy" with dns/base_url errors\- Regression test: onboarding automation end-to-end test that validates base_url propagation.

Issue 8: Unexpected tokenization/cost blowups\- Symptom: unexpectedly high token usage and bill increases.\- Root cause: prompts include large unseen context (user transcripts), or using full chat message history without summarization or truncation.\- Immediate workaround: recommend client-side prompt trimming and introduce max_tokens guard rails in examples.\- Permanent fix: add a cost-awareness section in quickstarts with code for rolling summaries and autosummarization integration.\- Detection: sudden per-customer token usage > 3x baseline in 24h\- Regression test: unit test that inspects token count for provided example inputs and asserts below threshold.

How to write a canonical fix KB article (template)

- Title: [KB] <Issue short description> — canonical fix
- Symptom: one paragraph
- Root cause: bullet list with references to repo/PR where fix will live
- Immediate workaround: steps for support agent to triage
- Permanent fix: step-by-step remediation + links to PRs + release notes
- Tests added: list of CI/eval tests added
- Rollout plan: staged deploy + monitoring queries to watch

Appendix: Doc checklist for authors and reviewers

- [ ] Uses the official SDK Quickstart or API Example template
- [ ] Includes runnable snippets for Python and JS (or marks language unsupported)
- [ ] Code snippets pass examples:test locally and in CI
- [ ] Performance & rate-limit guidance present where relevant
- [ ] Error handling section present with references to KB articles for top issues
- [ ] Includes owner contact and last_updated metadata
